cards.stem: Which phrase completes the inertia statement to describe when motion changes?
options: unless acted on by an unbalanced force
when mass remains constant
when velocity stays zero
during steady thrust
cards.quote: unless acted on by an unbalanced force
cards.hint: Recall the exception that lets motion change from rest or steady travel

cards.stem: How does the second law describe the link between acceleration, mass and applied force?
options: depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied
remains at rest in a straight line
exerts an equal and opposite force on the first
is inertia that resists changes
cards.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.
cards.hint: Think what two factors set how quickly velocity changes

cards.stem: What happens when one object pushes on another during an interaction?
options: exerts an equal and opposite force on the first
depends on the mass of the object
unless acted on by an unbalanced force
remains in uniform motion
cards.quote: Whenever one object exerts a force on a second object, the second object exerts an equal and opposite force on the first.
cards.hint: Consider the paired forces from mutual interaction

cards.stem: When is the familiar mass times acceleration form valid for relating force and motion?
options: only good for objects that have a constant mass
always valid for changing mass
requires an unbalanced force to start
defines inertia as resistance
cards.quote: Remember that this relation is only good for objects that have a constant mass.
cards.hint: Think when mass can be taken outside the change in momentum
